subject: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, liaison@acme-acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items

Team —

Attached two artifacts: a proposed rollout timeline (rollout_timeline_v2.xlsx) and a first-pass playbook (playbook-draft.md). I need a firm decision this week on whether we target a broad rollout on Apr 4 or a staged canary starting Apr 11. High-level tradeoffs:

- Apr 4 broad: faster time-to-value for ACME, higher risk on docs & enablement gaps.
- Apr 11 staged canary: gives docs + CS extra two weeks for training, smaller initial capacity footprint.

Please call out: 1) any must-fix doc/enablement asks, 2) infrastructure exceptions that would block Apr 4, and 3) an owner for the runbook.

ACME is asking us for a date to put in their launch comms by end of week (Friday). Kim — can you confirm any contractual SLAs that affect schedule?

Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Product Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollout_timeline_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), playbook-draft.md (markdown)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items

Ben — thanks for the clear ask. Quick notes from enablement/docs POV:

- Playbook-draft.md has the right sections but several owner gaps. We need named doc owners for: developer quickstart, SSO setup, and troubleshooting KB. I can patch the developer quickstart by Mar 23 if we scope to a lean version (examples + auth).
- Training: CS wants 72 hours lead time before a broad rollout to schedule customer training sessions. That pushes us toward Apr 11 for safety.
- Suggested owners: Developer quickstart -> laura_bennett; SSO KB -> marissa_cole; Troubleshooting KB -> kimberly_park (ops runbook overlaps).

If we proceed Apr 4, we should freeze the public docs on Mar 26 and ship a short “known issues and mitigations” addendum.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Developer Programs Manager

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items

Adding product readiness notes:

- Demo readiness: I can get a customer-facing demo script ready by Mar 24 if we keep the feature set for the demo to the baseline capabilities in the playbook. Anything beyond that (custom function calling examples requested by ACME) will require extra engineering time (~1.5 weeks).
- Feature flags: engineering has proposed a two-stage flag (canary + regional ramp). Ops will need a canary config and rollback playbook — tagging @dylan for details.
- Docs link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/launch/rollout_v2 (I added an action items page).

If ACME needs a date for comms, recommend we tell them Apr 11 and offer a potential earlier private pilot for priority customers (subject to Ops signoff).

—Marissa
Product Marketing

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items

Heads up — infra exceptions that impact Apr 4: we currently have a scheduled capacity maintenance window on Apr 2 for dedicated clusters in us-west that could affect throughput during the first week of Apr. Options: 1) move the maintenance earlier (ops-heavy), 2) postpone broad rollout to Apr 11, or 3) run a smaller canary on shared capacity where maintenance doesn't touch.

Jira: SUP-1234 tracks the maintenance and capacity scoping (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SUP-1234).

Kimberly — do we have SLA constraints or contractual obligations that force a firm date? If not, Apr 11 seems safer. Also tagging CloudVendor for confirmation on the maintenance window overlap.

Dylan
Senior Reliability Engineer

On Tue, Mar 16, 2027 at 08:22 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Adding product readiness notes:...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: liaison@acme-acme.com, integrations@cloudvendor.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rollout decision briefing and doc action items — Decision and owners

Team — after reviewing the inputs and the infra maintenance constraint, decision is to proceed with a staged canary beginning Apr 11 with the following concrete owners and milestones: 

- Runbook owner & lead runbook review: kimberly_park — deliver runbook.pdf by Mar 26.
- Developer quickstart & examples: laura_bennett — lean quickstart by Mar 23.
- SSO KB and troubleshooting: marissa_cole — initial KB by Mar 24.
- Canary checklist & ops readiness: dylan_brooks — canary-checklist.csv and capacity verification by Apr 4.
- Customer comms & demo: ben_carter — draft comms for ACME by Mar 19.

We will offer ACME an earlier private pilot (by request) subject to Ops capacity signoff. No contractual SLA requires Apr 4, per legal review, so the safer Apr 11 schedule minimizes customer impact and gives enablement time.

Action items summary attached (runbook.pdf, canary-checklist.csv). Please confirm owners on this thread and escalate any blockers by EOD Friday.

Kimberly Park
Release Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook.pdf (doc stub), canary-checklist.csv (csv stub)
